analysis.problem_summary: Determine whether a given integer n is a power of two.
analysis.intuition: A positive integer is a power of two if repeatedly dividing it by 2 yields 1 without encountering any odd factor greater than 1.
approach: Return false immediately if n <= 0, as non-positive numbers cannot be powers of two.
Iteratively divide n by 2 as long as n is even (n % 2 == 0).
After loop termination, check if the remaining value of n is 1.
Return true if n == 1; otherwise, return false.
analysis.why_it_works: Any positive integer can be represented as n = 2^x * m, where m is an odd number. Repeatedly dividing by 2 strips the 2^x factor. If m equals 1, then original n was purely a power of two.
analysis.key_takeaway: Repeated division reduces the input size exponentially each step, leading to logarithmic time execution without extra memory.
analysis.time_explanation: In the worst case, n is divided by 2 in each iteration, running at most log2(n) times.
analysis.space_explanation: The algorithm operates using only a constant number of primitive state variables without extra memory allocation.
